items.text:
>Since I don't know the "definitive truth" (by whatever rational definition one would assign to that phrase), I can't say.

Right.

>Do you really need to use your imagination to figure out whether you can afford both?)

Not to figure that out no. I can handle simple math without being creative about it since it is a learnt skill like reading. However I now have to rationalise. Which item is most beneficial to me to purchase? Who does it affect and why? Can I visualise what the consequences of my choices are? Can I imagine what will happen if I pick one over the other? 

I'm not trying to be smart here (I dare say you are a lot smarter than me), but I'd question your rationalisation in criticising how I think about truth if you yourself have no answers. That would be like a blind man trying to lead a blind man wouldn't it?

I found through suffering with anxiety that it really helped to focus on the 'now' and drag all my mental resources into dealing with just the things in my immediate present.
Anxiety is basically over-worrying about every little thing because you don't trust yourself or others to behave or act in an appropriate manner fitting with the circumstances you imagine. Trouble is we do this even though we are literally imagining these situations rather than what is actually happening in front of our very own eyes.
Maybe it's different for everyone and this tip won't help, but it may be worth a try?
This poem tells a fantastic story about moving from darkness to light. Thank you for this.

Free will does not involve limitless choices. We have boundaries. We cannot choose to travel at the speed of light for example. We cannot choose not to die.

We stand on a stage set and act appropriately according to the scene we are currently in. A righteous person will always act righteously. An evil person will always act evilly (is evilly a word? Haha).
Whatever anybody does seems right to them because they are following their nature. If asked who is in control of their actions, they would say 'I am' so we agree they act on their own choosing.

But the stage, the props and even the actors themselves were created by God for His pleasure and purpose. His ideas of things are way beyond our own understanding. He is the director, the producer and the author of life. We are actors ad libbing according to what seems right to us given the context of the scene but we do conform to God's will because nothing exists outside of it.

Our will exists in His domain. God is root. We are administrators of ourselves but God is root. He can terminate all running software and power off the machine. Even as administrators we can do that (suicide) but that would make us poor administrators if there was no good reason to power off.
It looks kind of like a surfing wave. Really beautiful.

items.title: Raw and Dirty
items.text:
Raw and Dirty
 I feel like I chipped away,  
 At the black hard dirt,  
 I was encased in.  
 Desperate to find,  
 Something I did not hate beneath.  

 How long this took!  
 How many years!  
 How often I said,  
 This is not all filth,  
 Surely not all filth!  

 My fingers are calloused,  
 My eyes are red,  
 I am black all over,  
 But I got there!  
 I found the diamond.  

 It's raw, a disappointment,  
 Born from unrealistic expectation.  
 And now I have to chip away harder,  
 Polish and cut, cut and polish,  
 Until I can finally be presented to you.
Yes. You got me.

I have six kids. You would think I'd have learnt after the first!
Total nightmare. They start getting smart mouthed, disobedient, run away to their friends houses, drink in the park, get in trouble with the police, steal your money, get tattoos, ah I could go on.

Still love them to death though. And they sort themselves out eventually if you keep reenforcing the disipline and boundaries.

In their very worst moment, in the midst of their very worst rebellion, I'd still not toss em in a lake of fire. They ain't bad kids really. Just same as us at their age.

The whole many gods concept is fatally flawed.
Who is greater than who? Who has the power over life and death? Who can judge who? Can an immortal being be made mortal by another immortal being?

Honestly it's just a total nonsense.

The only God I believe in is the one who holds the power over life and death. There can only be one or it just gets hella confusing.

Miracles? Seen a few with my own eyes. A non Christian mate came with me to a worship meeting to see what the hell was wrong with me.
He had driven a nail or something through his foot at work and it was really playing him up. He was limping with it and I felt bad for asking him to come out.
Half way through the meeting my mate who had looked bored as hell was suddenly all smiles and raising his hands in the air.
Turns out his foot just miraculously healed up. No sign of any injury. No limp. Nothing.

He refers to God as Big J now haha
Nah. Just the ones who refused to stop being idiots and carried on harming others even though they did know better. The ones who were truly wicked. The ones you would definitely agree needed to go.
He tries their whole lives but they don't listen.

> Do God's powers of persuasion without removing a person's free will end there?  This sounds like a limitation on his powers that people rarely talk about.

When the child rapist is raping the child and the child pleads with their eyes and their beaten mouth, that is God pleading. Now ask your question again.
Here you are blaming God and not the rapist. It is beyond understanding.

Casting a care is always such a welcome burden and it does so much good for you and by extension, me. Its a win win :)

You reap exactly what you sow. Always.

Maybe God is being patient. Storing up His wrath for the day when the victims will see their justice and rejoice with Him forever in an unending paradise filled with unending joy.
Maybe God just sees the bigger picture. I'd say its a fair assumption being that He's God and all.

> Are you interested in having a respectful conversation? 

I answered your question as I saw fit. I am sorry you didn't like my answers but I am not here to provide the answers you want but rather the answers I see fit.

Given this is your attitude I will not be engaging with you further.

> First, I cannot possibly fathom how you or anyone would think that the child needed to be raped in order to truly appreciate the reward that you (or God) are preparing for him/her.  

This is so blasphemous. No one needs to be raped! Let's assume God isn't rubbing His hands when wickedness occurs right?

>Second, until you (or God) share with us why you let the person rape the child to a satisfactory degree, you can at least understand why we think you are a complete jerk.  And, no I'm not blaming you for raping the child.  I'm blaming you for not doing a damn thing about it.

Rapists hide what they do. They threaten to burn the child's house down if they breath a word to an adult who cares. They threaten to kill their pets. They threaten to hurt their siblings, they threaten to hurt mummy.

Now if you've suffered this and still love God (as my wife did and does) why do you think you have a right to blame God for 'standing there watching' being all enraged about it, when the victim does not?

>And, no I'm not blaming you for raping the child.  I'm blaming you for not doing a damn thing about it.

I wasn't there or I probably would have cut his testicles off and sown them shut in his mouth.
As are you :)

(Not OP) 
I love this reply. I've always thought disregard is the opposite of love but contempt is stronger. It's like disregard with arrogance.

(Not OP)

There is definitely free will in heaven. Free will is an essential part of being a living being. We can use it for good or bad. In heaven you physically cannot sin but you can rebel and call faith into question for which you will be forced out.

Those who avoid the second death are the faithful. Those who sought love even as they were being hated. Those who turned the other cheek, those who put love beyond even their own personal safety. These are the gold that were purified by fire. They will be as lampstands in heaven and God Himself will light them up. They will rejoice with their God forever.

\> **What do you believe**

I believe God is love.

&#x200B;

\> **why do you believe it,**

 God proved this in Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ is the only name by which man can be saved. I believe it because I choose to believe it. I heard and I believed.

&#x200B;

\> **and what is your opinion of religious people that hate Atheists?** 

They are scared of addressing the often smart and well thought out questions posed by atheists because they are afraid that their faith may not strong enough to be able to answer conclusively and therefore they will let God down and  perhaps cause others to stumble in their faith. It is not the atheist they hate but rather the weakness of their faith. This get's projected as hate towards the atheist but in truth they wish the atheist to believe with even the little faith that they have.

I think that the universe is a little like that fairground in chernobyl. It was open for a very short while before disaster struck and then the entire thing was abandoned due to how toxic everything became.

If we were to live forever and multiply forever then we needed an infinite space to expand into. This is why the universe is like it is. It is however completely empty of humans with the exception of Earth where we began. When the bomb went off, God closed the gates. Sealed them up. What would have been trivial such as travelling at light speed with no concept of time passing between one place and another, became impossible for us due to our rebellion.

God will make a new Heavens and Earth for the faithful who rejected wickedness and lived in love. He has promised this.

Simulation? Perhaps our spirits step into sensory suits at birth so we can play in the environment and sense it as something beautiful and creative, real symbols of the Word of God so that we may know God in full.
Are you volunteering to give up your life and go help them? God will bless you if you do. If not I am afraid your judgement stands as though you accuse your image in a mirror.
Such a mature spirit and attitude. May you find all you seek.

If one partner is abusive and hurts the other I would encourage family intervention first. The father of the abused should challenge the abuser. If the father of the abused is dead or otherwise unavailable then a brother or someone who will defend the abused person's rights to live unmarked by violence, should intercede on the abused person's behalf.

If an apology and repentance can be reached so much the better. However if no agreement can be reached and no repentance is forthcoming, then the abused partner should go live with one who cares for them until such time that the abuser repents or divorces. The abused should not commit adultery during this time since this would negate repentance for the abuser who may well repent. 

Under no circumstances is God saying stay being abused in my name. It is a wickedness to suggest it.

If any of my daughters were being abused, they would have unlimited refuge in my house until such time that a decision had been reached by the abuser.

If the abuser decides to divorce my daughter, she is free to find love again if she wishes. I will not hold it against her and I will give her away myself.

You have every right to be angry. But how can you be angry with God?
Perhaps be angry with big pharmaceutical companies who keep profits and do not invest with the sickening sums of money they make from the sick? Perhaps be angry with the administrators who squirrel profits away for themselves and deny the funding doctors need?

Honestly, blame anyone but God. God does not rejoice in suffering. Ask Jesus.

The premise you are assuming here is that the abuser will remain faithful whilst seperated in an unrepentant state. Given the nature of the abuser is to seek someone to first flatter, then abuse, I dare say it won't be very long before they commit adultery.

My words stand as presented.

> Or you can just divorce them due to the abuse and move on right away.

Perhaps the abuser is living out the pain of being abused. Perhaps patience and understanding is required to save the marraige and restore it to be what it was intended.

In any case, the default position should not be to abandon the soul of the one whom you marry.

What if they were to see what they had done and wanted to make reparation?

As in all things, do what your conscience permits.

I merely state here the most beneficial position as I see it where forgivness is not ruled out from the outset. If God took your view, Jesus would never have come for us.
I already said what I would do if I were there.

Why do you think there is poverty? Do you think it is because the resources are not available to help?
How much have you donated? How many times have you visited these stricken areas?
Have you spoken with the warlords who take everything for themselves, even aid trucks sent to the needy?

You blame God but it is not God, who happily provides the resources freely. It is greed and money love that causes poverty. The poor pay for the rich. This has always been the case.

You misunderstand God's nature so your thinking is reasonable in context.

The truth is though, God makes His home in us. God completed all His work on the sixth day and took His rest on the seventh which is called Today.
God chose to live with us and in us *today*. We are His hands and feet. He is the Word. 

If you accuse God, you accuse yourself.

This is why I say when the child is pleading with the rapist whose conscience has been overridden with filthy lusts, this is God pleading. It is important to understand this. 

I know what you will say 'God is not limited in any way' but again you misunderstand. God's kryptonite is also His strength. God does not seek His own way. Love doesn't insist on its own way. It is the rapist who insists on his own way. 

God's Law is pretty comprehensive as to the penalty for ignoring your conscience and harming one made in God's image. 

Now the truth is we have all harmed another. None of us can claim we have not. Some harm may be minor whilst other harm, such as rape of a child, is very very serious. 

The penalty for any of it is death. You agree with God's law. You want the rapist punished. I want the rapist tortured and their body slung in a bottomless pit but what of our sins? Who will defend us when we are thrown in the pit? Who will intercede for us? 

Thanks be to God for Jesus Christ who takes away the sins of the world.

Perhaps you missed the part where I said do whatever your conscience permits?

I am not trying to bind abused spouses to their abuser. I have said seek refuge. Be patient. Patience would be folly if it waited forever. It won't have to. That's why it's a virtue. Have faith.

Oh please! Are you interested in truth or just appearing smart in front of 'the folks'?

 I am going through this exact situation right now with one if my daughters.

Her husband is bipolar and came off meds. He started acting up. Going crazy. Gaslighting and making up lies. Making her cry down the phone to us because she feared for their children.
She actually ran into another man's arms in a bid to feel loved.

Then the husband listened to our advice and went to see his doctor.

He is now on the mend and deeply regrets coming off his meds in the first place.

It was incredibly painful for my daughter to admit to us she had an affair (although she confided in her sisters readily).

My advice was to confess it to her husband.

She feared she would lose her children yet still she took my advice.

Upon confession he broke down and told her he didn't blame her. He blamed himself. So now they are both vulnerable and open with one another and their relationship is healing.

He sticks to his meds and we take more care to check in on him. It has strengthened us all.

If it were not for truth and compassion I dare say he would be dead now and his children would have no father. During his worst moments he woukd get filthy drunk and take his motorbike out at 100 mph. He is lucky not to be dead or in prison.

As for my daughters affair? Forgotten.

Until you have actual experience of these things, it is probably not wise to throw your 'intelligence' around about them.

His interactions can be seen most purely in the flesh of Jesus Christ. Jesus was pure and God's spirit in Him showed us how God is. There is no greater example of God making His home in the perfect man.

This same spirit wishes to live with us through our faith. When we are humble and obedient, then we do God's will on Earth as it is done in Heaven.

God made the world and rested. There is no more work to be done. The program is running. The developer is resting from all His work of creating.

Our choice is to rest with Him or destroy what He has made. Love or hate. But whatever we choose, we reap exactly what we sow.

>For God, helping people would be easy. For us humans it's much harder.

Is this an excuse not to donate? You are God's hands and feet on Earth.
If your conscience is clear then it is God's will.

I just asked my 12 year old. Told him someone on the internet wanted to know. He gave me a look as if to say 'Is that a real question?'
I nodded solemnly. He sighed. He said 'If someone has a mental personality disorder and kills someone, then no not God's will obviously.'

He's a bright kid. I expect he will go a long way.

We think of love as being an emotion and indeed we do experience a feeling of love in our emotions but love is more than that. Love is a doing.

Love is giving up your place in the queue to an old lady who has a heavy basket.

Love is giving up that seat on the train you never thought you would get in the first place, to a pregnant lady.

Love is getting up at 5am to take your boys to football practice.

Love is holding your wife's hand when she is tearing chunks out of it during labour.

Love is about putting yourself out of pocket so that another less fortunate may profit from your generosity.

Love is swimming into a dangerous place to rescue someone drowning.

Love is dying on a cross to pay for all mankind's sins even though you yourself are totally innocent, hoping God raises you up again and that your faith was justified and that your brothers will be set free and will be ressurected even as you hope you will be.

I am not trying to be obtuse in anything I say :)

Ill take your understanding. Thank you.

>I like how you assume that I don’t have experience with abuse. 

Well if you have some personal experience and you think it is topical, please share as I have done. It adds to the discussion when there has been real skin in the game.

>I also like how you ignored my statement on being complacent with abuse. 

I did not intentionally ignore anything. I am tired. Been a long day. I will review after this.

>Were the police never called? Come on! She was fearing for her children’s lives! We’re her children around her abusive husband? 

Abuse takes many forms. People who suffer mental abuse often say they wish it were physical so they could prove it. But abusers often enlist family members to help unwittingly with their gaslighting. 'She's acting up again. I don't know why she's so moody and angry with me' 
Then family members take an active stance against the abused pushing her further into hell. 

In my daughters case, she was fearing for her kids having a responsible adult in case she had a nervous break down. What could she do? Phone the police and say 'my husbands thinking all kinds of crazy things about me cheating on him. He won't let me out the house. Wants me to quit the job I worked so so hard to get. Monitors my every call, text whatever'? 

No. What she did was run into the arms of someone who cared about her at work. Someone who fell in love with her and wanted to run away with her. 

Then it was discovered that the husband had gone off his meds. I mentioned he was bipolar right? Quite manageable. 

Back on meds and he feels like an idiot. He forgave my daughter and apologised for being stupid with his meds. She now makes sure his schedule is followed. The kids are over the moon (my granddaughters are a treasure :)) because mum and dad are happy again. 

It could have all been so different. I'm glad it worked out like this.

Jesus came as a human being to be where we are. For Jesus each day was 'Today' and God was still resting since there was no day after the seventh. Jesus wanted to follow His Father's instructions to the letter. Our Father is resting.
Jesus was completely faithful to the instructions He was given by His Father and therefore God's will was complete in Him. All things were made through Him then since He was a trustworthy source and given the title King of Kings. If Jesus is the root of the tree, we are saved through Him. His ability to do miracles was based on a conviction that God had provided for Him so as not to make God look like an idiot through Him. And God did provide. Obviously. Even the ressurection of His only begotten Son who was crucified under false testimony that those who believe in Him may not perish but receive eternal life.

> For every situation like your daughter's there are two more that end horrifically. What can you say to that?

Lets say worst case scenario, the spouse had no one they could trust and no money at all to escape. What options do they have?

Since we are talking on the Internet we shall stick to modern civilisation options rather than living in a cave community for example.

Well as you mentioned, there are authorities that can help. The police would put you in touch with those authorities. Shelters for abused marraige partners and so on. Somewhere you could go to be safe and get your head together so you can figure out what to do next. These places exist.

Lets say none of those services exist nearby or are not accessible. What about a neighbour? Someone, anyone. Reach out. That would be my advice.

The reason family members want reconciliation is because once you both stood there before them and made promises to eachother on your big day. They see there must have been something good or what were you doing there?

No father however wants his daughter to suffer beyond what she can bear. If the husband is a pig then pigs do as pigs do and she won't have to suffer him long. That will be a mercy for both father and daughter.

Right. I don't see it that way. I'm saying bad things do happen and we have to do what's right for us by listening to the voice that's for us and not against us. Do what your conscience permits.

It sounds like you had a rough time. I am sorry that happened. I hope you are on the mend. I hope you have friends to help you.
Bless you
Pick a number. Any one...
Just take little steps and remember to take stock of your positive progress. Keep a diary. It really helps.

>Could God use people with mental personality disorders to fulfill His will?

Nothing is impossible for God.

>If someone were to commit what the average Christian would consider a sin with a clear conscience, are you saying it's God's will for them to sin? Or would it indicate that they have a mental personality disorder?

Christians are just lost broken people who found hope and are trying to live according to that hope, using the strength they find in that hope. Christians ought be aware they live by grace and should not judge another living soul.

>Was your point in relaying your interaction with your son to try to belittle someone by making them feel less reasonable or intelligent than a twelve year old? Because that's how it came off to me, at least.

Yes because the context was entirely appropriate.

Happiness is often misconstrued. I know what it is to be happy when I have not known where my next meal will come from and I have been equally happy living in absolute luxury. Happiness is being content no matter your situation.

This is not the easiest of states to achieve without faith. Faith says "Ill be alright no matter what' and actually believes it! And guess what? You are alright no matter what. Every time your faith proves genuine, you get even more confident you will be OK. You thank God. God blesses your faith more. Your contentment becomes full over time as you no longer worry about your life and how you will survive. This isn't to say you dont have to work. Even the birds who don't worry that God will provide for them still have to get up early and dig.

God definitely rested on the seventh day of creation I.e today and every moment since the end of day six.

What you are getting confused over is what is defined as active work in the present.

If I compress a spring and clamp it today and go to sleep and someone takes that spring whilst I sleep and unclamps it, then the work in the spring is released even though I am asleep.

How someone uses that stored energy is up to them. When I wake up I may say "where is my spring and what did you do with the energy stored in it?' 

How you answer will determine whether I will be angry or delighted. Even if you wasted the energy nothing is really lost right so I can be merciful and not acknowledge the trespass and forgive you?

Now creation definitely did have error handling built into it. No programmer worth his salt would ignore the possibility of user error. If the error is fatal we log it and shutdown gracefully.

I have no idea how the Spirit of God impregnated Mary, just that this was part of God's will and Mary did not reject it. Note how God sends messengers to explain to Mary why He chose Mary. Mary was found to be suitable to bear God's Son because she had faith in God and trusted God. But the ins and outs of it I don't profess to understand. It's a miracle for sure. But it is important to the story because it determines the purity of Christ's flesh which was to be presented unblemished as a sacrifice for our sakes revealing God's complete and unconditional love for us.

I know context is hard for some people but do try and keep up.

We are talking about a clear conscience in normal healthy functioning people obviously. Adding a straw man says more about where you thought it was heading and that you didn't like it at all. 

You think this about point scoring but to what end? I just speak my truth. That's it. I don't have any expectations of how it will be received. I just hope people don't misappropriate the context I speak in. If they do, I try to correct.

A cult typically follows a charismatic person . 

The church follows a charismatic person in Jesus Christ.

Jesus died for what He believed in.

Cult members sometimes die for what they believe in.

&#x200B;

So whats the difference? The difference is in the taste of the fruit they bear  upon following the convictions of the teachings of their leader. One tastes bitter, the other sweet. One leads to eternal life, the other to God knows what?

items.title: Gold for a Bumper Sticker
items.text:
Gold for a Bumper Sticker
[removed]
Taste it and see.

If it tastes good and provides nourishment for you soul then you can be confident that it is for you.
If it tastes bitter and does not help you then it is not for you and is motivated by something else.

If something is for you, how can it be against you? If that something is God who lives forever , then how can He suddenly not love you anymore and cause you to perish?

>So your soul is you mood or your mental wellbeing?

The soul keeps a record of loves lost and won. The more loves won, the better the mood and mental well being.

>What are you seeing and what does it tell you about a soul? Do you think how an idea makes you feel is a good standard for wether or not it's true?

Happiness, sadness, disbelief, anger, light, dark. All these things.

I can only speak of what I believe to be true based upon my experiences. You don't have to believe me. Yiu have every right to challenge and I have every right to stand firm. 

>Or maybe I don't know if there's good reason to believe a soul exists because I've not seen evidence or a good definition of a soul.

Ok
A kind of memory yes. But one in which we store eternal things.

\> How do we know anything stored in the soul is eternal? 

Faith
No we do not know. It is a matter of faith. A hope. Because we love.
How do you know it doesn't get you any closer to the truth?

Well if I put my faith in God even though I want to doubt because I want to handle my own stuff thanks, and my faith is not proved false, I can be confident that there is a higher power who has my best interests at heart. That I am loved and considered even though I really wanted to ignore the conviction that comes about through faith because I wanted to be in control of everything concerning me and not consider what was actually best for me. The conviction that comes about through faith is life to me honestly.

>So you've not given any reason to think faith leads to true beliefs.

If you saw what I was before faith and what I became after it then even as skeptical as you are, you would say 'Wow! I dont know what that kid is on but boy has it turned his life around!'

>And not proved false is a pretty terrible standard. It leads you to accepting contraditory statments which can't both be true because neither has been false yet.

What kind of contradictory statements are you referring to? I have not once been let down for not seeking my own way and following the conviction of my faith. In fact the only time I stumble is when I try to ignore the conviction. That happened a lot in my early walk with Christ. Thank God He was/is patient.

It's only in your head that I have destroyed my own argument because this is your desire. You invent a straw man to back up your assertion and muddy the context.

That's fine. Whatever makes you happy. It doesnt change what I am saying or it's validity in the cold light of day.

As much as I enjoy our little dance (and I feel I know your every well timed step now), I feel the music has come to an end and we must kiss eachother on the cheek and depart. I bow my head and go seek out the cheese and crackers :)
I'd like an authors commentary. I've read it several times and I'm slipping a gear somewhere because I'm missing it's message. I want to understand though.

> Remarriage after divorce is never allowed. 

 Were you not married to the world before you became a Christian? Were you not forced to divorce yourself from it in order to prepare for your marraige to God with the Spirit preparing your skirts?

If I in good faith marry a woman who then takes many lovers and I divorce her, am I then expected to remain alone? Is it good for man to be alone?

The divorce nullifies the promise in these circumstances. I am not bound to the promise because the one I made it to did not value it and did indeed reject it. My promise is voided and I am free to choose another.
So when Jesus says except in the case of fornication, do you ignore that?
Got ya! Thanks for opening it up for the stupid :)

> Are you blaming OP for the problem of children that are born in poverty stricken countries with cancer?

Not at all but neither am I blaming God. I am blaming greed.

>Can OP have *prevented* that situation from occurring?

No but he could help alleviate it and in doing so would help his own conscience which clearly he is troubled by since this topic is in the forefront of his mind.

>Let's say OP has dedicated their entire life to helping those in this exact situation. Would OP's judgement of God then stand?

No it would not stand and the OP having seen with his own eyes what is actually the cause of these problems would have to agree. Go speak with the warlords. Go with the UN Peacekeepers and try negotiate with them regarding what they consider to be theirs by rights vs everyone elses rights. It's eye opening.

>Edit: I just realized this isn't one of the debate subs, apologies, not intending to debate on the wrong forum.

It's fine. I am a Christian and you asked a Christian :)
I like the way this flows with the dead breaks punctuating the irrationality. Its really good.

Yeah appreciated. I did struggle with the title as you probably realised :)

Let the non Christians write what they want. Hey if they win they win :) 

 I will repost with your suggestion.

&#x200B;

Thanks for your help

The messenger has free will of course although angels will conform to God's will as His obedient servants. God knows who He can trust. But ultimately everything is God's creation and He made literally everything for His pleasure and purpose. Everything will conform to its purpose because every little thing is covered.

Let's say the messenger decided they wanted to follow Satan's way and disrupt the program. Well that will be covered too. Every little thing is covered. Every little thing. If you think you can outsmart the program you are very very wrong. There's an if for every but.

It is my position that any claims of 'We are the One True Church' is the same as creating factions in the body of Christ and it should be terminated.
The body of Christ is the one true church and scriptural differences, unless blatantly heretical, should be cast aside as they are not useful for building up the members of the body. Only love in the Spirit of God should be acceptable to the members. Not factions and divisions.
Thank you :)

Ok, so your main point is about the Eucharist and from my limited knowledge this was the key point in the split?

Here's the thing though. I have never taken communion in a physical church setting. I don't even care about it. I don't even go to church.

As far as I am concerned, Jesus' body is the bread of life, and his blood is the sweet wine we drink deep of... In Faith. In Faith.

Coming Up
I took a deep breath and dived under,

There was nothing for me up top,

I heard scared voices beseeching me,

Begging me to stop.

&#x200B;

As my feet slipped beneath the surface,

I was encased in a watery grave,

I kicked towards the bottom,

I was feeling very brave.

&#x200B;

As big fish eyed me warily,

And the smaller ones did flee,

The bottom became closer,

And my heart did fill with glee.

&#x200B;

After some time I did reach it,

The bottom of the trench,

Strange things they did grow there,

Among the sulfurous stench.

&#x200B;

I marveled at their strangeness,

Their ability to survive,

Such pressures at this depth,

The depth that I did dive.

&#x200B;

No one knows you're here I thought,

As I watched them watching me,

Who considers these marvelous creatures,

That dwell at the bottom of the sea?

&#x200B;

I waved goodbye and kicked my legs,

My lungs had had enough,

I headed for the sun again,

Fear not, I'm coming up!

&#x200B;

How? One way He could do it would be to just roll up creation I suppose. Destroy everything He made. But that seems a bit defeatest for an Almighty God right?

I'm not selling anything. I am calling for unity among the brothers and sisters of Christ, saying put away silly squabbles and live to love, but you're not buying it. It doesnt matter a blimp to me whether you think I'm some hermit Christian, fake Christian, making it up in my head Christian or whatever. What does matter to me is speaking my peace which I have done here.
What about childbirth? Is impregnating your wife immoral?

> Your god, as described, could eliminate suffering and still accomplish his goals.

This is just incorrect. Did you have a choice to be born? No. So for arguments sake let's assume a first creator who made the human tree somehow. Some sentient being who just is. Nothing proceeds him. He is who he is.

This being has the power to bring forth living beings whom he calls creatures.

So he brings forth living beings by the power of his word.

Now what of those creatures? Are they now not slaves to the first creator? If they are to be free creatures ought they not also have the choice to not exist? Should life be conferred upon a being and that being have no say in it? No! I ought have the choice to accept or reject life now that I AM here. I choose life obviously. Its cool right? But what if no choice was given? What if the first creator made everything perfect and installed his  creatures in this perfect place and made them behave perfectly by programming them to be perfect? Think of Eden with only the tree of life. Off you go guys, here's the tree. Eat from it and live forever perfectly. A group of us look at each other. What's the alternative here folks? So we walk ahead and live forever and never look back. Honestly this thought fills me with revulsion.
Imagine not being able to say 'err excuse me first creator dude but I don't want to play this game you dreamed up. Looks cool and all but nah, if you could switch me off mate that would be great.'

A living being must be given choice. It is a pre-requisite of lawful creation.

So men choose what they will. But since choice has been given, God must be patient so that all men have a chance to choose life. The reason we are not terminated the moment we sin is because God is compassionate and wants to give us the chance to seek Him. Jesus became the bridge between man and God through His body. Sin did seperate us from the Holy Father, the first creator. All of us. But Jesus buried our sin in His sinless body. The first creator showed His power through Christ's ressurection. If we have the Son, we have the Father. This is choosing the tree of life with the alternative being death which we have already clearly chosen since sin separates us from holiness which currently sustains us by grace and patience. As long as we are breathing we have a choice.

>But you don't. You don't have the choice to cease the existence of your "immortal soul."

I do though. If I reject the very source of life, I no longer have life. I disappear as if I never existed. The ultimate penalty for sin is death. Eternal death. No ressurection. No second chance. A bottomless pit of non existence. To reject life is to reject love. If you truly love your mum for example, how can you bear the thought of being seperated from her ever? Love rejects this idea of seperation. It will accept absence but not eternally. It saves what it loves.

>This is just some kind of random assertion that doesn't have to be true. 

But logically it does have to be true. Lawfully. This universe is highly ordered. Laws exist that govern everything. Laws are super clucking important. I cannot be forced to exist lawfully. If God is love as I claim, how can any loving being force me to be? Don't I have a right to not play this game? If I don't have the right because some first mover says so, then where the hell does his authority come from? There must be some authority at play here right? I am not being conferred rights to die. Who had this authority to force me to live? This is a great injustice. My personal hell where I am forced to live forever even when I don't want to!

So choice is lawful. Period. It is necessary for lawful creation of living beings. 

>Except you don't. You can't choose to sprout wings and fly, and you can't choose not to be born with original sin, and you can't choose to have your immortal soul not exist.

God's covenant written in His Sons blood says you are free to choose life in Him. Repent and be saved.

>Plus this whole rant operates under the assumption that there is no freedom of choice in heaven.

Heaven itself is the object of choice. You choose Heaven. Jesus holds Heaven in His hands and offers it you. If you choose it, you choose the tree of life from the offer of both trees that are being presented you. 

You can choose perfect. It will not however be conferred upon you. God does not seek His own way. You have a choice.

Depends whether you have understood who God is. If you have not understood, then that will not be held against you. If you have lived to others and not yourself and have lived in love whilst not knowing its name then you will be rewarded and be offered the chance to eat from the tree of life.

If you have known God's grace and you reject it then you yourself would testify that God was good to grant you your request for eternal death since you did reject the life you were bestowed with for free.

Hell for the believer is that state of being eternally seperated from God. The thought of it fills us with terror. Thankfully for us we know our souls are safe because Jesus Christ guarenteed them. This is the whole good news bit.

> I don't understand what you mean by eternal separation. If I cease to exist, it's not a separation.

Not from your perspective. It was your desire.

But from the believers perspective however, your choice is unfathomable and literally scary as hell. We believe and desire in eternal life with our living God whom we know now by His Spirit who was sent to us to help us upon believing in the name of Jesus Christ who lives forever.

Not existing is the most disgusting thing we can imagine now that we have tasted the good things God has to offer. But it is eternal life He offers. We run away from death into the arms of life. Death is hell for us apart from Him.

First Love
I remember my first love,

I think I was four,

A girl with pretty curls,

All sweetness for sure.

&#x200B;

Her round little cheeks,

Rosy red from the sun,

I was quite convinced,

That she was the one.

&#x200B;

I wouldn't have shared her,

Not for the world,

The only kindness,

In a life that was cold.

&#x200B;

I convinced her to run,

Hold my hand, not look back,

My intentions were good,

Some biscuits I packed.

&#x200B;

We set off at pace,

Heading God knows where,

But we were stopped by the road,

Knowing danger was there.

&#x200B;

It was my greatest failure,

We had to turn round,

Walk back in shame,

Eyes down at the ground.

&#x200B;

For the rest of the day,

We played in the street,

I loved her so dearly,

I forgot my defeat.

&#x200B;

Some time later,

My parents moved home,

And I cried at the thought,

Of being alone.

&#x200B;

Though time moves us onward,

On the wings of a dove,

I still remember fondly,

That girl, my first love.

&#x200B;

&#x200B;

&#x200B;

&#x200B;

Love does not seek its own way.

>He would be better off going home and just meeting people naturally, and waiting till they asked about his faith.

I admire his conviction to preach and they might have been open to it. But given that they were not, he should have bowed out gracefully, not sought his own way on the matter.

>Theologically, he seemed to think that the message of the cross ( the death, burial and resurrection ) was the gospel.

This message Paul considered of first importance as well. I agree. 

1 Corinthians 15:3-8

THE RESURRECTION OF CHRIST

3 For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, 4 and that He was buried, and that He rose again the third day according to the Scriptures, 5 and that He was seen by Cephas, then by the twelve. 6 After that He was seen by over five hundred brethren at once, of whom the greater part remain to the present, but some have 2 fallen asleep. 7 After that He was seen by James, then by all the apostles. 8 Then last of all He was seen by me also, as by one born out of due time.

I honestly have no idea what you mean by any of this. Is this because I have a carnal mind?

What is the message of the Gospel in simple terms according to you? A message spoken in such a way even a child could readily understand it?
He would have done better armed with donuts, coffee and less of an 'i dont care how you feel' attitude though don't you agree?

(Not OP)

Perfect response imo
What does that mean?

No ones against you pal. No ones gonna get banned here unless you act up and break subreddit rules consistently I imagine. 

If you speak the truth, how can there be anything to overcome it? You would not fear speaking the truth.

What is this answer you fear will get you banned?

You have carte blanch to offend me under my own post. I would ask moderators to permit it. I certainly permit it. Please feel free to enlighten me or offend me. Its all the same to me. Truly.

The Father : Let's make creature versions of us.

The Son : We have to give them free will.

The Father : Of course. 

The Son: Which means they are free to choose evil and therefore death. 

The Father: Yes, once they become living beings they must not be forced to exist by our will alone.

The Son: But what if they do evil by mistake?

The Father: Then the evil they do must be repented of and atoned for.

The Son: But how will they repent if they don't know right from wrong.

The Father : I will set my Law before them.

The Son: But this will bring them death since the Law is unforgiving and must be obeyed.

The Father : Then you must become the fulfillment of the Law on their behalf.

The Son: I must guarentee their lives you mean?

The Father :Yes

The Son: I offer all that I am to guarentee their lives.

The Father : You understand what this means?

The Son: Yes

The Father : So be it. Let there be light....

Sorry if the message wasn't clear. I am trying.

The Law is unforgiving because it does not permit evil of any kind. Evil doers are put to death because it would be a greater evil to permit evil to do evil forever than to destroy it.

The Law protects the lawful and condemns the lawless.

But what of mistakes? What if we are lead into sin by one with their eyes open?

It would be evil not to forgive such a person who stumbled in this way, since they were tricked into giving up their lives.

But the law doesn't care about motive. It is unmoveable in every regard. It must be this way or their would be no justice for those it serves to protect.

But the Law is not greater than those it serves to protect. And those it protects may issue mercy to those that trespass against them. There is no law against forgiving.

So the person forgiving fulfills the purpose of the Law which is entirely based on 'love your neighbour as yourself'.

So what's the sacrifice for? Why does Jesus need to come and be a sacrifice?

Well forgiveness is fine but the evil has already been done and has consequences. The consequences are that God's creation had been adulterated with evil acts. There is now blood in the soil and all manner of filthy unclean practices. Flesh has partaken in every unclean practise and is itself unholy and must not be permitted to live forever.

Our flesh must be put to death. It cannot enter eternal life.

So how does God atone for us? How can we be made clean again? We literally need to be born again but how? We cannot climb back into our mother's womb right and then pop out all new and fresh.

So we need to be made entirely new. A brand new creation. The old must be put to death because it is no longer fit for purpose. 

So the guarentee from God's only Son is His body and His blood. 

If all fails, the Son offers His body to clothe us in and his blood to give us new life to live in His body. 

If all fails, we have refuge in Him. He is the atoning sacrifice which takes away the sins of the world and puts them to death in His own body. He takes the full punishment of the Law meant for everyone upon His own shoulders. He loves us even though we did not know His name. 

The Father cannot ignore the blood poured out for us. Jesus must be ressurected since there was no sin found in Him and if Jesus is ressurected, we know the Father approves of Him and we can trust Him. If we claim it (the body and the blood) , we have both the Father and the Son and are declared clean before God. The law has to set us free because it had no further claim against us and because Jesus was the first to be ressurected, we can be confident that we will be to since the power sin gets from the Law to destroy us, is no longer in effect for those who have clothed themselves in the righteousness of their sinless Lord. 

We who are in Jesus are sons of the Most High God through faith in His Word, may He reign forever.

>Here is a list of some of the unbiblical doctrines commonly propounded by Christianity:

>The trinity

In the beginning God does not say 'I will make living beings in my image' 

He says 'Let us make living beings in our image' 

Jesus is the Son of God. A Son must have a father and indeed Jesus calls Him, Our Father. And He is our Father when we are welcomed into His house by the Son who is not ashamed to call us His brothers. 

When Jesus is not present, God's spirit is sent to help us. If Jesus is present, the Holy Spirit will not speak in His place. 

The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are God, the one God in three persons. A Father is not a father without a begotten child. A child is not a child without a sire. No love can exist that represents this relationship without the relationship existing. The Holy Spirit is the love between the child and the father. This is why the Holy Spirit was blown into the Apostles before Jesus departed. So that we may know the Father through Him when we believe on His name. 


>The immortality of the soul

Agree, utter horse poo unless you are saved and confess Jesus as Lord. Otherwise its perishing time. 

>Heaven the place of reward for the righteous

Perhaps you are being a little pedantic? 

Living by the light of God and the Lamb forever will be paradise. 


>Hell the place of eternal torment for the wicked

Well refusing God's gift means you want to pay for your own sins. Bear your own punishment. 
Imagine receiving punishment free from grace before being destroyed. What a horrible ending. Still it was a choice. 

>That Christ died instead of us, rather than for us (substitutionary vs representational sacrifice)

Again feels a little pedantic. I know what you are saying but in many cases the message is not lost because of the slight difference in meaning.

For example Jesus did die instead of us. If He hadn't, I would still have to bear the punishment for my own sins. This alludes to the fact that Jesus took a heavy burden from me. This is true. The fact that my sin was represented in Him and that it was actually me put to death is a slightly harder theological concept to grasp. It's the solid food if you like whereas the other is closer to breast milk. 



>That the (english) "Devil" and "Satan" refers to an angel who sinned and fell from heaven

Revelation 12:7-10

Then war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back. 8 But he was not strong enough, and they lost their place in heaven. 9 The great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil, or Satan, who leads the whole world astray. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.

This is a scriptural truth is it not?

>Let me stop you right there. Why? This makes no sense whatsoever. Evil without evil motive isn't evil. And punishing evil committed without evil motive isn't justice.

Lets take an example.

Lets suppose I don't know stabbing babies is wrong. I just like the squishy noise the knife makes as I plunge it in and out of their soft little necks. Their blood feels pleasantly warm on my hands.

The Law doesn't care. It wants me incarcerated so I cannot continue to do evil.

The Judge on the other hand will take motive into account but will still agree with the law. My sentence would be held in a place where I could be educated, medicated and helped but so I could never be in contact with babies again. The law just cares that I am never in contact with babies again.

>Again, what does that mean? Do you understand why that kind of language irritates me? If the point you're making is meaningful why you can't explain it in regular English?

It means that God's spirit lives in me. That I see that God loves me despite my own appetite for self destruction and because I see how much I am loved (God would push my drunk ass out the way of the oncoming bus even if that meant Him getting hit in my place) I start to adopt God's attitudes towards me and show them to others. I live to others because I follow Jesus. I'm a bit rubbish at it but I'm learning.

>Which isn't justice. The point of justice is you punish the person who did something wrong. Punishing someone else is in no way comparable. It's an empty metaphor. The explanation boils down to "the atonement is like justice, except that it's completely different."

The atonement is a mercy. Mercy is greater than anger. Mercy may be issued because I am ignorant or I beg for it with a sorry heart. If I am forgiven then I am forgiven. If I'm not, I'm not.

>I also object to the way you're anthropomorphising the law. That's another meaningless metaphor. The law is not a person, it's a set of rules, and can't give sin power or set people free.

The Law is a decree. It is issued by intelligence. It is a righteous decree. God's law is righteous. The law cannot set any transgressors free. But it contains the penalties for sin and the penalty is ultimately death. It cannot save anyone. Only the Judge can do that.

> Anyone who doesn't know stabbing babies is wrong is either mentally disordered (which, you will be interested to note, is a legally valid defence) or wilfully ignorant (which is just as evil as the crime itself). So yes, in so far as your point is relevant the law does actually care.

The law doesn't care. It just wants the harm removed from babies. The Judge cares. He is the one interpreting the law and seeing how it best fits the case. Even where mental impairment is a defense, it is a defense against what? It is a defense against the accusation that the Law has been transgressed. It is up to the Judge to decide. Not the law. If the law could decide then the police could lock you up without question and no judge would be necessary.

>Mercy implies a just punishment that is averted, so this doesn't affect the point in any way whatsoever.

Do you morally object to being shown mercy?

>Exactly. So every anthropomorphic behaviour you attribute to it is the moral responsibility of the intelligence, right?

Anthropomorphic descriptions are merely grammatical constructs to aid in visualising quite difficult concepts. I am not sure why you have such an objection to it?

What are you looking for?

>Actually it does... 

Sure, addendums have been incorporated in to the written law of the land to allow judges to make caveats with guidance from the lawmakers themselves. But these are caveats. The Law of God at its heart says love your neighbour as yourself. The penalty for not doing this is death. The law is quite specific in this regard hence we all die. All the logic in the world cannot escape death.

>Well no, because they'd be ignoring the part of the law which you for some unfathomable reason don't count as part of the law.

The police walk in and I'm covered in blood and a pile of dead babies at my feet. I'm licking the blood off the knife and urinating on the pile of flesh.

Not one policeman is going to refer to any law book. I'm gonna be locked up and thrown in a van. I'm going to be imprisoned and I will await trial because of due process. But according to you I am innocent because of mental capacity so why do the police even bother with me? They don't care anything about my mental capacity. They just want me to stop causing harm. The Judge can work out what to do with me.

>No, why?

I don't really understand your position on it.

>that's contradictory, because the Law-giver and the Judge are in your view the same person.

A judge can show anger or mercy can they not? Mercy is greater than anger no?

> And being mentally deranged and stabbing a baby violates that law to a lesser extent than *not* being mentally deranged and stabbing a baby - if indeed at all. So I still don't understand why you're arbitrarily excluding that provision from what counts as the law proper.

What difference does my mental state make to the parents of the victim? Is there pain any less?

>So, they're taking a temporary precaution while the law takes its course, which - incidentally - the law also provides for.

What would the father of one of those babies do if he walked in on me just as I am about to murder his firstborn? He has a gun in his hand. Is the father interested in my mental problems? Does it persuade him to show me mercy and allow me to plunge the knife into his precious baby? Or does he shoot me on sight when I don't drop the weapon? 

>But then I'm no longer sure what you mean by "the law". With respect, it seems to mean whatever is convenient to you at the spur of the moment.

I am not interested in proving what I believe in myself to you. I am merely expressing what I believe using things that can be understood and debated. If I speak purely in spiritual terms you will say I am talking nonsense. If talk in terms of God's law, you will say that my argument is invalid because justice and mercy are incompatible as though God Himself were schizophrenic. 

If I talk in terms of law of the land, which you understand, you will say I am switching from talking about God's law to suit myself. 

>My central question is why substitution serves justice. Saying that the atonement is an act of mercy doesn't get around that question.

Just as no justice was received for the husband whose wife committed adultery that Jesus set free from the mob holding stones, we too must recognise that we have all sinned and have to give up the right to justice too unless we too want to receive the full measure of wrath for our sins as well. 

Whatever we permit, is permitted us. Whatever we deny is also denied us. 

But the law is immovable. If we have all sinned there is no hope for us if we keep condemning eachother for the trespasses against us. And this is what we do. We keep demanding justice despite not repenting ourselves. 

Jesus says look... Whatever you have done, you may be forgiven. Forgive eachother as God has forgiven you. 

And we say 'How has God forgiven us? What did we do to God?' 

And God says 'whatever you do to eachother, you do to me' 

And we may say 'but what is that to you? Can we enter heaven and hurt you God? How can we, little specks of dust, hurt the Almighty God?' 

And He may say 'Everything that is proceeds forth from Me. Everything belongs to me. If anything is broken, it must be paid for' 

And we may say 'if everything comes from you, what can we offer as payment?' 

And God will say 'I have already paid for the things you broke as a favour to you, a favour that you did not deserve' 

And we may say 'How Lord? These things were yours! Why did you have to pay for what is yours?' 

And God says 'because the transgressors were already in debt and I must have order.' 

So how did God pay? With His own Son's blood. A holy offering to pay for the unholy. The law cannot refuse it since it is the fulfillment of the law. To love your neighbour as you yourself would wish to be loved. Jesus would want to be saved if in our shoes and is not false. He is faithful to His word. 

So now we may say 'So are we free to go?' 

And the Lord may say 'I set you free' 

The Law is satisfied in every respect. 

And the upshot? We understand what true love is. We were in the dark before.

> This is completely irrelevant

To you maybe. It is not to me. We can agree to disagree.

>Obviously, protect his child. The father isn't executing the law.

But he is. He is loving his child as he would want to be loved. He would want to be saved from the murderer as well if he was in his child's shoes.

>Firstly, *please* stop doing this. The law isn't a person. If you mean God, just say God. This is needlessly ambiguous. It serves only to obscure the fact that what you're calling the law here is an arbitrary set of rules *imposed by God*.

Please don't tell me how I should debate. I speak as I see fit, not to coddle to your sensibilities. You may have success elsewhere with these tactics but they will not wash with me. If you want to dispute, go ahead, but understand I don't care if you are offended by anything I say or how I say it. I just couldn't care less. I'd be annoyed if what I said didn't offend you. You hate Christianity and seek to tear it down. I stand against that. Be offended. 

The rules are not arbitrary. They are based on a single important principal which I have discussed in this thread many times. Love your neighbour as you love yourself. 

>there are plenty of ways of fulfilling this which don't involve brutal torture.

Please enlighten God. I'm sure all the tears Jesus shed when saying not my will be done but yours will be considered worthless in light of your great revelations.

>. Can we get back to the debate please?

I'm waiting for your answer to my last question. Tell me how you solve the problem of evil?

Assume I am a servant of God come to take a message back to Him about how it could be that Jesus did not need to suffer a hideous death.

I have outlined why He did. Now you must provide a rebuttal in the interest of debate.

You have asserted that no brutal torture was needed. I would like to take a message back to God from you. So what is it? How would you do it differently?

>People who have done nothing wrong, or who have committed sins in genuine ignorance, should be let off.

They are let off. Living beings not yet old enough to know right from wrong have no culpability other than to their parents who may discipline them as they see fit. A four year old child who dies in a car accident does not have the right to eternity denied them. This is a stupid Christian myth and nowhere does the bible back up this false claim.

People who commit sins in ignorance are also not held accountable. Jesus Himself shows God's will in this area by saying 'Father forgive them for they know not what they do'. They will be shown mercy. 

>People who have done wrong should be punished commensurately, or, if God wishes, shown mercy and let off.

Agreed. 

>Why is showing mercy easier because an innocent person has been tortured instead?

Because the innocent person was God Himself. He came as a human being. There could be no claim against Him that evil was allowed to prevail and He had shown an indifference to it. 

God cannot be indifferent to evil.

But if God were to destroy evil, we would all need to be destroyed for all have sinned (even the four year old who slaps his little sister in anger because she has received a present for her birthday and is jealous).

So to show He isn't indifferent, He takes our punishment on Himself. In full. Willingly. For our sakes. If we see this and believe it, we see God's love for us in full. It causes contrition. We don't want to be responsible for it. We don't want to keep on sinning, giving God more reason to suffer us in patience. It changes us from the inside out.

The Law is blind. The Judge's decision in how to apply the law is not. This decision is based in love.

The Law says Thou shalt not commit murder.

And yet here I am giggling in urine and blood and dead babies.

God sees I am ill. God prescribes some outcome that satisfies the Law. I need to be kept away from babies. I need help. It would not be fair to put me on death row. Everyone would complain. But incarcerated I will be. There will be no freedom for me. But I am deserving of mercy from death. 

>You're using a word which has a specific meaning (retribution exacted on a guilty party) in a context where it cannot have that meaning. You're basically saying "the Atonement is like punishment except that it's completely different". That's the metaphor I don't understand.

There will be those who do evil with their eyes open. They do it in spite of love. They prefer it. They reject love with open eyes. They see the truth and then double down on the evil they do. They will never repent. 

They will not receive grace. They will have the full punishment of the Law exacted against them. This means they will suffer according to the measure that they dished out and then they will be terminated. Similiar to being stoned to death. Pain, pain, pain, extinction. 

The rest of us live by grace. There are those who are decent people for the most part, you for example. If you were to reject eternal life and God's grace and wanted to take your own punishment, I dare say what you suffer as a punishment would be minimal and commensurate with your sin. But you would still get your wish to be terminated. You would not be ressurected after this termination. No second chance. 

Then there are people like me who have done bad stuff and have repented to God. Have cried in fear for my soul because of what I have done. Have cried out to Jesus and asked Him for help. I have no way of undoing the things I have done. How can I escape the death I am due? Who will save me? I cannot save myself. I am destined for destruction but I want to live. I want to change. I want a second chance. How may I earn my salvation? Should I punish myself? Should I try and be good now? Would that be enough? These are not things I can go to prison for, but they are wicked things. Like no one in the civilised world goes to jail for adultery but it is a soul destroyer nonetheless. Not that I've commited adultery either but I use it to illustrate the point. 

My problem is I have no opportunity to make things right. The damage is done. I cannot undo it. I agree evildoers should not be allowed to live forever so effectively I am on death row with no hope for clemency. 

So Jesus says 'hey roguedeath, I hold the keys to life and death' 

I am like 'How Jesus? What right have you to confer life or death? Doesn't the Law decree I must die. How can you be above the law? ' 

And Jesus is like 'I have defeated the power of sin to harm you by putting it to death in my body' 

So I say 'How Jesus mate? How can your death do anything for me? It's me the Law wants to terminate, not you! I am evil, but you're not. How could you ever be put to death lawfully when you are sinless anyway?' 

Jesus says 'If I offer to take your punishment on your behalf, what's that to you?

And with regards to how I could be put to death lawfully? You are right. It is impossible. But false testimony would suffice. I would accept it as my Father's will that I would act as an everlasting sacrifice for my brothers, pleasing to God.' 

'I don't understand Jesus' I say. 'How is this pleasing to God?' 

Jesus says 'Sacrificing myself to save you is a supreme act of love and it is blessed of God. If you hold dear to my example, pick up your cross and follow me, you will not perish but receive eternal life.' 

So now its about faith, hope and love. Nothing else.

You have to understand why punishment is exacted in the first place.

Punishment is eye for an eye, life for a life. Punishment should not extend beyond what is due. It is for the lawless that this is written. The lawful have no need for these written laws at all if indeed there was no lawless person left! People who live to others and not themselves, who act kindly and considerately, these people are lawful people.

I dont need to know about eye for an eye because the thought of plucking out someone's eye fills me with absolute revulsion. I'd never do it.

But if someone plucks out my eye unlawfully then I am grateful to the Law because it speaks to justice.

It's says to the lawless person 'So now we will take your eye because you had no right to take another's. As you have done, so will be done to you'

So I am standing there watching the state appointed doctor holding his gillette sharp spoon and the eye thief is strapped to a gurney.

'Please mister' cries the eye thief, 'please mister I am so sorry.'

Now what should I do? There's the question of my one good eye. It's gonna affect me my whole life. It is going to be a pain.

But honestly, this guy seems genuinely sorry. And the gillette spoon is making me feel sick. I don't want to watch. I don't want to hear him screaming as the spoon slips through the nerves severing the glistening orb from his body.

I say 'stop. I forgive him!'

But it's not up to me. This is the punishment due to the lawless. But my word should count right? I've said don't hurt him. It's OK, I forgive him. But the Law is not interested in my forgiveness. It is only interested in punishing the lawless. It hates lawlessness.

So what of my forgiveness if I cannot even save the man?

How do we satisfy the Law so that my forgiveness makes it back off?

Well what does the Law require? An eye for an eye right?

What will happen if I offer my other eye to pay for the first that was stolen?

Well the Law will tell me that to take my other eye would result in another trespass so it is not permitted. 

I say, no one will take it. I myself will give it. 

The Law is in a state of confusion here. 

Justice is being superceded here by something else. Justice is being superceded by sacrifice. Justice exists for the benefit of the lawful, a deterrent for the lawless. The deterrent is imperative. Someone's eye has to come out or the lawless will think God has gone soft on crime. An eye is being offered so someone will be punished as a deterrent. 

So now we have to go to the lawmaker himself for guidance because we have stepped outside of its boundaries. 

I say to the lawmaker, 'let me be the example you set to those who would take an innocent man's eye' 

And the lawmaker might say 'but you are the victim. How can you offer your eye to pay for the one that was stolen?' 

And I might say 'what concern is it to you if I do this?' 

I am fulfilling the Law. I am offering an eye for an eye albeit to cover the sins of another. 

Now you may say 'well the eye thieves are going to be delighted with this. They get to steal your eye with impunity, why should they care that you offer your other eye?' 

And I would say 'if they are not repentant then I will let them face the full extent of the punishment the Law decrees, however if they repent and are genuinely contrite and prove it by stopping being eye thieves, then I will do for them this undeserved favour'

> You should try your hand at horror fiction. Some natural talent.

I love horror fiction. It's probably entirely plagiarism haha

>Yeah, but then the premise fails. If you have a way of distinguishing genuine contrition from false contrition the deterrent is just as effective.

Sometimes it is only witnessing the consequences of our actions that is needed to spark contrition. Not all evil people are naturally evil. Some are lead astray. Some are coerced into sinning by naturally evil people. 

The cross seperates the chaff from the wheat very very effectively. It is utter genius in my eyes. Honestly it makes me marvel more than all the galaxies in all of space (and I've spent enough time pondering the mysteries of space!)

Breathe Me In
    Your worry tugs on my nerves.  
    "Come here" it whispers into the air.  
    "Comfort me."  

    The water is dangerous here.  
    It spirals downward.  
    "Come here."

    Ive negotiated these waters before.
    I am not dead yet.
    "I am coming."

    Now you lay in my boat.
    It sits silently.
    "I am here."

    You hold me closer. 
    Letting it go. 
    "Breathe me in."

>All they know is "Hear, O Israel, the LORD our God is ONE Lord."
